title: Precedent record
description: Chapter 5, Definition 8. Append-only: records are added when cases resolve and never removed.

case.description: The case that produced the record.

prov.description: The provision the record is filed under. This is the retrieval key.

rules.description: The full set of provisions the case touched.

premise.description: The subset of facts on which the holding rested. This is the input to distinguishing: distinguish(r,c) holds exactly when premise is not a subset of facts(c).

auth_class.description: The ordering key. riskowner outranks judges; all adjudicative instances are equal.

auth_id.description: The individual who resolved, so that attribution is a fact of the record and not of the configuration.

width.description: Smaller is narrower. Incomparable domains tie.

depth.description: Deliberation depth. The final tiebreaker only.

expiry.description: Mandatory on every risk acceptance (A7). Null on interpretive records, which do not age out by clock.

cites.description: The record this one is filed against. Carries two obligations: a renewal must name what it renews, and a record departing from an earlier holding on the same provision must name that holding. A newer record that conflicts and is silent displaces nothing.

admission_ground.description: clause_i: contested and resolved above first instance. clause_ii: the representative of a consolidation class. seed: opening jurisprudence, admitted at deployment, whose neutrality cost is priced by the admission theory.
